t: A port on the Elbe that grew from the Carolingian Hammaburg and a twelfth-century merchant town into the Hanse's North Sea gateway.
Neutral behind its walls in the Thirty Years' War, it became the largest and richest city of northern Germany and a centre of music and theatre.
Annexed by Napoleon and wrecked in 1943, it survives as a city-state of the Federal Republic and Germany's largest port.
dyk: Hamburg celebrates its port's birthday every May on the strength of a charter of Frederick Barbarossa dated 1189 that historians have shown to be a thirteenth-century forgery.
ev: Date of the Barbarossa charter, later forged, that underpins the port's privileges
Hamburg and Lübeck ally to protect the road between them
Bugenhagen's church order brings the Lutheran Reformation
Denmark recognises Hamburg as a free imperial city in the Gottorp Settlement
The Great Fire destroys about a quarter of the old town
Operation Gomorrah's firestorm kills around 35,000 people
Hamburg becomes a state of the Federal Republic of Germany

f.founder: Count Adolf III of Schauenburg (merchant new town, c. 1188)
